checkpoint: retained polynomial sign refinement and complete constant Sturm chains
retained_change: Polynomial sign queries reuse the existing retained parameter refinement state and build the filter Sturm chain only once per query. The separate raw-isolator sign entry point and its duplicate bisection loop are deleted. Hypersolve accepts a certified nonzero constant as a complete one-row field Sturm chain without trying to normalize its zero derivative.

exactness.reproduced_failure: Before the solver fix, a constant pi filter at the selected root of 2t^2-1 returned Uncertain(RealSign), and the direct nonzero-constant Sturm regression failed. Both pass after the three-line field-kernel fix.
exactness.retained_certificates: The selected-root GCD proof, non-root interval endpoints, checked Sturm root counts, exact midpoint witnesses, and retryable uncertainty remain authoritative. A common polynomial factor outside the selected interval does not certify a zero at the selected root.

sign_regression.coverage: Both policies; simple and even-multiplicity roots; a common root outside the selected interval; filters rooted at either or both endpoints; midpoint filter cuts; shared selected roots; nonzero constants; rational and pi scaling. Repeated sign queries populate the retained source certificate; a source midpoint root needs no source Sturm chain.

constant_chain_regression.coverage: Positive and negative pi, sqrt(2), and rational 5; zero, one, or two trailing structural zeros; both policies. Every chain has one terminal coefficient, zero variations at -1, 0, and pi, and zero roots in [-1,1]. Empty and all-zero polynomials remain rejected.

exactness.unbounded_refinement: The retained regression separates sqrt(1/2) from half the 104th continued-fraction convergent of sqrt(2), requiring more than the retired 256 bisections. Both measured variants use the same regression fixture and pass it.

source_size.scope: Formatted physical source lines in the two implementation commits. Hypercurve's parameter production prefix shrinks from 4,334 to 4,288 lines. The removed offset import is test-only; moving and simplifying its existing deep-refinement fixture plus adding the boundary matrix grows test code by 45 lines. Hypersolve adds 34 test lines and three production lines. Reports and this checkpoint are excluded.

measurement.method: A six-repository archived workspace freezes dependencies. Identical new test fixtures were added before building and preserving the baseline executable; only Hypercurve's production sign-refinement changes were then applied for the candidate. Both artifacts were confirmed rebuilt. The constant-field solver fix is deliberately excluded from this isolated performance comparison; full correctness validation uses the final workspace revisions.
measurement.production_prefix_hash_scope: The first 4,288 lines of candidate bezier_parameter.rs, before its test module, match the final checked-in production source.
measurement.command: /usr/bin/time -v taskset -c 7 bash -c 'for sign_filter_iteration in {1..1000}; do <variant executable> bezier_parameter::conversion_tests::algebraic_sign_filter_has_no_fixed_refinement_cap --exact > /dev/null || exit; done'
measurement.repetitions: Three alternating batches per variant; 1,000 independent test-process executions in each batch. An exact-filter dry run of each executable confirms one test executes and passes.
measurement.caveat: Each batch includes process and libtest startup. The machine was not exclusive; batches received 95-96 percent CPU. These measurements describe this deliberately deep refinement case, not a general workload speedup.

linked_size.workload: bezier_algebraic_parameter benchmark executable, excluding unit-test code
linked_size.benchmark_source_note: Both frozen variants use identical benchmark source. Only rustfmt line wrapping differs from the checked-in benchmark.
linked_size.scope: Matched frozen dependencies, benchmark source, and feature/profile settings. No matched library-archive baseline was preserved, so no rlib-size claim is made.
